camps.name: NW Ridge Camp
camps.why: Timberline tent sites on the lower ridge at about 7,500 ft after a bushwhack from Remmel Lake; sleeping here leaves a few hours of climbing to the summit.

camps.name: The lower Chewuch River camps out of Thirtymile
camps.why: These break the long walk in from the road before the Remmel Lake bushwhack; they are approach camps and are not slept at on the two days this plan counts.

plan_conflict: The plan starts and ends at Remmel Lake, so it leaves out the long walk from Thirtymile in and out, which adds nights for a party starting at the road.

camps.name: Four Point Lake
camps.why: Several good tent sites at 6,850 ft with Remmel in view, about 15 miles in. Sleeping here makes the summit a light day trip, and there are trout in the lake.

camps.name: Upper Cathedral Lake basin
camps.why: The base right under the Monk and Cathedral, with short walks to either. It suits all three nights after the long first day; keep tents on durable ground away from the shore.

camps.name: Andrews Pass
camps.why: About twelve miles up, the halfway stop for a late start or a split of the long walk in. It adds a night and pushes the Monk day back by one.

camps.name: Cathedral Pass benches and the tarn slabs
camps.why: A high, windy bivy on rock and thin turf at the crest for a pre-dawn start. It skips the drop into the lake basin but offers little shelter.

camps.name: Copper Glance Basin camp
camps.why: Tent sites around 6,600 ft by a small tarn in the upper basin, about three hours from the trailhead. It leaves roughly 2.5 hours of climbing to West Craggy.

camps.name: Copper Glance Lake
camps.why: A lower camp near 6,100 ft that shortens the walk in but adds extra gain on summit morning; most parties continue to the tarn sites higher in the basin.

plan_conflict: Copper Glance Lake was marked main on file, but climbers report sleeping at the small tarn camp near 6,600 ft in the upper basin, so the basin camp is now main.

camps.name: Horseshoe Basin — Sunny Pass, Louden Lake and the Smith Lake meadows
camps.why: Established sites in the trees near Sunny Pass keep Windy Peak close with water nearby. The open tundra camps and Loudon Lake lie about a mile farther and are more exposed.

camps.name: The Tungsten Creek trail camps below the Boundary Trail junction
camps.why: Forest sites near the Chewuch junction and up the lower Tungsten trail, a first night that leaves about six miles and 2,000 ft for day two. Bugs are bad in the valley.

camps.name: Tungsten Mine Camp / Boundary Trail #533 junction
camps.why: Old mine cabins and flat ground at 6,750 ft, about a mile from where the west slopes begin. Two nights here give a light-pack summit day; the cabins are shelter in a hailstorm.

plan_conflict: The on-file notes call the Tungsten Creek trail camps the second night, but the plan reaches Tungsten Mine Camp on night 2, so the lower camps serve night 1.

camps.name: Pyrites Creek — where the Chimney Peak approach leaves the trail
camps.why: Bear wires and several tent sites about nine miles in, where the off-trail climb begins. It spares the extra four miles each way to the chalet but offers no toilet.

plan_conflict: The plan sleeps both nights near Enchanted Valley Chalet at 13.5 miles, while the camp on file is Pyrites Creek at about 9 miles; the research found no climbing report that settles which.

camps.name: Enchanted Valley Chalet (emergency shelter and camp area beneath the peak)
camps.why: A permitted camp area on the valley floor at about 2,000 ft, below the south wall. The summit day starts here; the price is a 14-mile walk in from the road.

camps.name: Ten Mile Camp
camps.why: Roomy riverside camp with big trees, about 10 miles in. A comfortable first night and the easy last night before the final walk out.

camps.name: Lake LaCrosse and Hart Lake — the base for Mount La Crosse and White Mountain
camps.why: Lake camps above the valley for the pass-side climb. Hart Lake has no privy or bear wire, so carry a canister; bears are seen around both lakes.

plan_conflict: The plan sleeps nights 2 and 3 by the river at the La Crosse Pass junction, which matches no camp on file, so the lake camps are used here as the nearest listed option.

camps.name: Honeymoon Meadows Camp
camps.why: The usual base on the West Fork Dosewallips, about 14 miles from the road end below Anderson Pass. Expect a river ford and heavy bugs; the summit day is then a light-pack push.

camps.name: Lake LaCrosse and Hart Lake — the base for Mount La Crosse and White Mountain
camps.why: Reached from the Duckabush side, a different and longer approach. Use it only if you come in that way, since this plan's Dosewallips route does not pass it.

plan_conflict: Lake LaCrosse and Hart Lake was marked main on file, but it belongs to the Duckabush approach and this plan sleeps at Honeymoon Meadows.

camps.name: Heart Lake
camps.why: The last camp on maintained trail with easy water, just under 8 miles in. The summit day from here is very long, nine to twelve hours, but it saves a cross-country carry.

camps.name: Cat Basin
camps.why: Sleeping here or at Cat Peak brings the Catwalk and Carrie closer and shortens the summit day, but the way beyond carries no water, so fill up first.

camps.name: Boston Charlie's Camp
camps.why: First camp past the Catwalk, at the foot of Carrie's southwest ridge for the shortest summit day. The only water is a poor pond that needs a good filter.

camps.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort campground
camps.why: A drive-in campground near the trailhead for the night before day 1; it saves a rushed start after the long drive and is not slept at during the trip itself.

plan_conflict: Cat Basin was marked main on file, and reports show parties camping at Cat Basin or beyond the Catwalk to shorten the summit day; the plan's Heart Lake base is the long option, so Cat Basin is now route.

camps.name: Cat Basin
camps.why: The last sheltered ground before the route leaves the trail, below Cat Peak. A good first night that puts the Catwalk next morning; fill every bottle before leaving the divide.

camps.name: Boston Charlie's Camp
camps.why: First camp past the Catwalk, at the foot of Carrie's ridge, which gives Fairchild a single long day over Carrie. The only water is a small pond that must be filtered.

camps.name: Eleven Bull Basin and the Cream Lake cross-country camps
camps.why: Meadow with streams beneath Carrie and Ruth, the natural night for parties moving on along the range. It lies beyond this plan's Boston Charlie's base.

camps.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort campground
camps.why: A drive-in campground near the trailhead for the night before day 1; it saves a rushed start after the long drive and is not slept at during the trip.

camps.name: Deer Lake
camps.why: About 3.5 miles up, a stop for a late start, but you still have the climb to the High Divide ahead the next morning, so it adds a long second day.

camps.name: Heart Lake
camps.why: A last camp on maintained trail with easy water, just under 8 miles in. It gives a shorter first day than Cat Basin but a longer second day over the Catwalk.

plan_conflict: Eleven Bull Basin and Cat Basin were both main on file; the plan sleeps Cat Basin on night 1 and Boston Charlie's on nights 2 and 3, so Eleven Bull becomes route.

camps.name: Glacier Meadows
camps.why: The base for Blue Glacier climbs, 17 miles up the Hoh, with 11 sites and a pit toilet. Reserve a permit; the glacier is a short walk above and you cannot camp between camp and the ice.

camps.name: Snow Dome high camp
camps.why: A designated high camp on the rocks of Snow Dome that shortens the day to Glacier Pass, but it is exposed with only meltwater, and you carry full glacier kit up to it.

camps.name: Heart Lake
camps.why: A first-night camp on trail with easy water, about 8 miles in, and a comfortable return night after two long off-trail days.

camps.name: Eleven Bull Basin and the Cream Lake cross-country camps
camps.why: Meadow camp with running streams beneath Carrie and Ruth, giving a light-pack summit day. It is the usual camp for Ruth without the full traverse.

camps.name: Cat Basin
camps.why: The last sheltered ground before the cross-country route. Sleeping here on night 1 gets you over the Catwalk next morning, but the way beyond carries no water.

camps.name: Boston Charlie's Camp
camps.why: First camp past the Catwalk with poor sinkhole-pond water; a closer but drier alternative to Eleven Bull that is better placed for Carrie than for Ruth.

camps.name: Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort campground
camps.why: A drive-in campground near the trailhead for the night before day 1; it saves a rushed start after the long drive and is not slept at during the trip.

camps.name: Anderson Tarn high camp
camps.why: A few sites on the Anderson Glacier moraine near 5,100 ft, with a tarn for water, about a mile above Anderson Pass. It puts the Thumb a short day away; arrive early for a spot.

camps.name: Honeymoon Meadows
camps.why: About three miles below the moraine camp. A night here splits the 17-mile first day but leaves the climb to the pass in the morning, and the camp is buggy.

camps.name: Enchanted Valley and Anderson Pass — the approach to Anderson's Thumb
camps.why: The long Quinault-side approach with staged camps on the East Fork. This plan comes in by the Dosewallips instead, so it is used only by parties crossing from that side.

plan_conflict: Honeymoon Meadows was marked main on file as the usual base, but this plan walks past it on day 1 to the moraine camp.

camps.name: Upper Ferry Basin / Ferry Glacial Lake
camps.why: High basin camp at about 5,700 ft among moraine and meadow, reached after Stephen Lake; a tarn on the crest gives water and starts the push toward Bear Pass.

camps.name: Elwha Basin, Queets Basin and the upper cross-country bivy zones
camps.why: Cross-country bivy sites near the head of the basins, the working camps for Barnes. Plan on dry, grassy meadow ground and stash overnight gear for the summit trip.

camps.name: Lillian River and Mary's Falls — the first night out of Whiskey Bend
camps.why: A first-night stop on the Elwha approach from Whiskey Bend; not used on this plan, which starts at Sol Duc, unless you reverse the traverse.

camps.name: Hayes River and Elkhorn — the mid-valley camps, and the base for Mount Norton
camps.why: Level mid-valley Elwha camps for parties walking in from Whiskey Bend; this plan does not pass them, since it exits to Whiskey Bend in a single long day.

camps.name: Chicago Camp — the last established camp in the upper Elwha
camps.why: The last trail camp on the exit down the Elwha. A party that cannot finish the 32-mile exit day stops here rather than pushing on.

new_camps.name: Cat Basin
new_camps.why: The staging camp for the traverse, below Cat Peak before the Catwalk; parties bivouac in a clearing short of the ridge and fill every bottle first.
new_camps.notes: Elevation not confirmed in research. Reports of the traverse put the first night here or at a clearing just short of the ridge up to Cat Peak.

new_camps.name: Stephen Lake
new_camps.why: A beach or snow-edge camp on the lake after the Catwalk and the long traverse; it makes a natural second night, and Stephen Peak is an optional side trip.
new_camps.notes: Elevation not confirmed in research. One traverse account camped behind a snowdrift at the lake on night 2.

plan_conflict: Nights 4 and 5 sleep at a meadow near Bear Pass, which no camp on file names; the Elwha Basin bivy zones are the nearest listed camp, and the on-file Elwha camps belong to the approach from Whiskey Bend.
